title: Same-year regional detections improved California fish-larva predictions, but prior-year detections gave no clear gain
abstract: We tested whether prior-year regional detections improve local fish-larva predictions beyond temperature and local history. We used 59 CalCOFI labels, 927 held-out spring tows and 20 test years in 2000-2022. Models fitted only earlier years. Adding the prior-year detection fraction at other stations gave a mean log-loss gain of -0.004269, with a three-year block range of -0.014448 to +0.005952. No-trend and other-sector checks also gave no clear gain. A later same-year diagnostic improved log loss by 10.21 percent beyond the temperature model, or 7.95 percent without a trend. The paired same-year advantage remained positive with log and Brier loss and one-, three- and five-year blocks. Same-year models use other held-out catches and measure interpolation, not advance prediction. Regional catch patterns carry same-year information, while this simple prior-year indicator did not reliably improve later predictions. Catches do not measure latent occupancy or dispersal supply. Water masses, spawning and survey conditions can produce the same pattern. We do not estimate a causal fraction of the thermal tracking gap. Code, hashes, aggregate results, figures and instructions are included; external records stay outside the bundle.
